items.title: The Annunciation
items.meditation: The angel Gabriel said to Mary: "Hail, full of grace! The Lord is with you. You will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall name him Jesus." Mary answered, "Behold, I am the handmaid of the Lord. May it be done to me according to your word." (Lk 1:28, 31, 38)

items.title: The Visitation
items.meditation: Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit and cried out in a loud voice: "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. At the moment the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the infant in my womb leapt for joy." (Lk 1:41-44)

items.title: The Nativity
items.meditation: While Mary and Joseph were in Bethlehem, the time came for Mary to give birth. She gave birth to her firstborn Son, wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn. (Lk 2:6-7)

items.title: The Presentation in the Temple
items.meditation: When the days of purification were completed, Mary and Joseph took Jesus to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord. Simeon blessed them and said to Mary: "Behold, this child is destined for the fall and rise of many in Israel and to be a sign that will be contradicted; and you yourself a sword will pierce." (Lk 2:22, 34-35)

items.title: The Finding of Jesus in the Temple
items.meditation: After three days, Mary and Joseph found Jesus in the Temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions. He returned with them to Nazareth and was obedient to them. (Lk 2:46, 51)

items.title: The Baptism of Jesus in the Jordan
items.meditation: Jesus, the sinless One who became sin for our sake, descended into the waters of the Jordan. The heavens opened, the Father's voice declared him to be the beloved Son, and the Holy Spirit descended upon him for the mission he was to fulfill. (Mt 3:13-17; 2 Cor 5:21)
items.fruit: Gratitude for the grace of Baptism

items.title: The Wedding at Cana
items.meditation: At the gentle prompting of Mary, Jesus changed water into wine. This was the first of his signs; he revealed his glory, and his disciples began to believe in him. (Jn 2:1-12)

items.title: The Proclamation of the Kingdom
items.meditation: Jesus proclaimed the coming of God's Kingdom and called everyone to conversion. He forgave the sins of those who approached him with humble trust, a ministry of reconciliation that he entrusted to his Church. (Mk 1:15; 2:3-12; Lk 7:47-48; Jn 20:22-23)

items.title: The Transfiguration
items.meditation: Jesus was transfigured before Peter, James, and John. The Father commanded the astonished Apostles to "listen to him." This revelation prepared them to accompany Jesus through the Passion and toward the glory of the Resurrection. (Lk 9:28-36)

items.title: The Institution of the Eucharist
items.meditation: At the Last Supper, Jesus offered his Body and Blood as food under the signs of bread and wine. In this mystery, he showed his love for humanity "to the end" and anticipated the sacrifice he would offer for our salvation. (Mt 26:26-28; Jn 13:1)

items.title: The Agony in the Garden
items.meditation: Kneeling, Jesus prayed: "Father, if you are willing, take this cup away from me; still, not my will but yours be done." In his anguish, he prayed more earnestly, and his sweat became like drops of blood falling on the ground. (Lk 22:42, 44)

items.title: The Scourging at the Pillar
items.meditation: Pilate released Barabbas to them. After having Jesus scourged, he handed him over to be crucified. (Mt 27:26)

items.title: The Crowning with Thorns
items.meditation: The soldiers wove a crown of thorns and placed it on Jesus' head. They put a reed in his right hand, knelt before him in mockery, and said, "Hail, King of the Jews!" They spat upon him and struck him on the head with the reed. (Mt 27:29-30)
items.fruit: The reign of Christ in our hearts

items.title: The Carrying of the Cross
items.meditation: When the soldiers had finished mocking Jesus, they led him away to crucify him. On the way, they took hold of Simon of Cyrene and laid the cross upon him to carry behind Jesus. (Mt 27:31; Lk 23:26)

items.title: The Crucifixion
items.meditation: When they came to the place called the Skull, they crucified Jesus. He prayed, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do." Darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour. Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Father, into your hands I commend my spirit." (Lk 23:33-34, 44, 46)

items.title: The Resurrection
items.meditation: On entering the tomb, the women saw a young man who said to them, "Do not be amazed! You seek Jesus of Nazareth, the crucified. He has been raised; he is not here. Behold the place where they laid him." (Mk 16:4-6)

items.title: The Ascension
items.meditation: After speaking to his disciples, the Lord Jesus was taken up into heaven and took his seat at the right hand of God. (Mk 16:19)

items.title: The Descent of the Holy Spirit
items.meditation: Tongues as of fire appeared and came to rest on each of the disciples. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages as the Spirit enabled them. (Acts 2:3-4)
items.fruit: The gifts of the Holy Spirit

items.title: The Assumption of Mary
items.meditation: "Arise, my beloved, my beautiful one, and come! You are all beautiful, my beloved, and there is no blemish in you." (Sg 2:10; 4:7)
items.fruit: The grace of a happy death

items.title: The Coronation of Mary
items.meditation: A great sign appeared in the sky: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars. (Rev 12:1)

prayers.title: Sign of the Cross
prayers.text:
In the name of the Father,
and of the Son,
and of the Holy Spirit.
Amen.

prayers.title: The Dominican Way of Praying the Rosary
prayers.text:
℣. Hail, Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with Thee;
℟. Blessed art Thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of Thy womb, Jesus.

℣. O Lord, open my lips;
℟. And my mouth will proclaim Your praise.

℣. O God, come to my assistance.
℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

℣. Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, and will be forever. Amen. Alleluia.
prayers.rubric: (In Lent, replace “Alleluia” with “Praise to You, Lord Jesus Christ, King of endless glory.”)

prayers.title: Apostles’ Creed
prayers.text:
I believe in God, the Father almighty,
Creator of heaven and earth;
and in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord;
who was conceived by the Holy Spirit,
born of the Virgin Mary,
suffered under Pontius Pilate,
was crucified, died, and was buried.
He descended into hell;
the third day he rose again from the dead;
he ascended into heaven,
and sitteth at the right hand of God the Father almighty;
from thence he shall come to judge the living and the dead.

I believe in the Holy Spirit,
the holy catholic Church,
the communion of saints,
the forgiveness of sins,
the resurrection of the body,
and life everlasting.
Amen.

prayers.title: Our Father
Hail Mary
prayers.text:
Hail Mary, full of grace,
the Lord is with thee.
Blessed art thou among women,
and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

Holy Mary, Mother of God,
pray for us sinners,
now and at the hour of our death.
Amen.

prayers.title: Glory Be
prayers.text:
Glory be to the Father,
and to the Son,
and to the Holy Spirit.

As it was in the beginning,
is now, and ever shall be,
world without end.
Amen.

prayers.title: Fatima Prayer
prayers.text:
O my Jesus, forgive us our sins,
save us from the fires of hell;
lead all souls to heaven,
especially those in most need of thy mercy.
Amen.

prayers.title: Hail, Holy Queen
prayers.text:
Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy,
our life, our sweetness, and our hope.
To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.
To thee do we send up our sighs,
mourning and weeping in this valley of tears.

Turn then, most gracious advocate,
thine eyes of mercy toward us,
and after this our exile,
show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

prayers.title: Pray for Us
prayers.text:
℣. Pray for us, O holy Mother of God.
℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

prayers.title: Concluding Rosary Prayer
prayers.text:
O God, whose only-begotten Son,
by his life, death, and resurrection,
has purchased for us the rewards of eternal life;
grant, we beseech thee,
that meditating upon these mysteries
of the most holy Rosary of the Blessed Virgin Mary,
we may imitate what they contain
and obtain what they promise,
through the same Christ our Lord.
Amen.
